Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Glyph Head of ML), Evan Ortiz (Glyph Platform Eng), Samir Rao (Glyph CTO)

Auto-generated summary:
- Follow-up on morning reliability incident: short window of 5xx responses + timeouts under burst. Discussed root-cause hypotheses (proxy vs model runtime vs rate-limiter), retry/backoff tuning, and next steps for packet-level logs and a benchmark run.
- Agreed next actions: share logs/timeline, validate proxy retry settings, run a focused latency/5xx benchmark on Dedicated pool if needed.

Topics: reliability incident, 5xxs, timeouts, rate limits, retries, KV cache behavior, Dedicated vs Hosted fallback, observability logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: ok hey everyone thanks for joining the sync, today main agenda is follow up on the incident from this morning, quick round‑robin intros – Alex from Redwood, Priya SE, and on the customer side Maya, Evan, Samir
[00:18] Maya: yeah thanks, to recap on our side, at ~09:12 local we saw a spike of 5xxs across our edge, essentially for about six to eight minutes, roughly 4% of requests in that window returned 502/503, a lot of timeouts reported by the mobile app and lambda consumers
[00:38] Evan: adding, our front‑end proxy (we're on istio + nginx hybrid) had CPU spikes and we also hit a rate limit at our API gateway, we had the retry logic but it was pretty conservative so apps surfaced the error
[00:55] Priya: ok thanks, curious — do you have request IDs or a trace slice? that helps correlate to the Redwood side logs, also did the errors map to a single model version or across variants?
[01:11] Maya: mostly to the redwood:openai‑like model alias we pinned for the test, looks like both v1.2.0 and v1.2.1 had errors but uhh slightly more on v1.2.1, although transcription/labels maybe off because our client sometimes maps differently
[01:30] Samir: we also saw a lot of retries from the client which amplified the backend load, so the classic retry storm question, we have a 2x exponential backoff currently but initial retry wait is 200ms, maybe too short for cold starts?
[01:50] Alex: yeah that aligns with our preliminary telemetry, we saw sudden connection churn and some 5xx at the load balancer layer, initial hypothesis is interplay between proxy timeouts, client retries and a small window of longer model latency due to KV cache misses during the burst
[02:12] Evan: side note — our infra team adjusted a circuit breaker to failfast at 10s which may have produced some 504s as well, that confuses the ladder a bit, apologies if the names are weird in the logs
[02:30] Priya: totally, can you share the proxy config snippet? even a small difference like idle_timeout vs upstream_timeout can flip behavior, also what are your client retry caps per route?
[02:45] Maya: I'll add that in the slack thread, posting the gateway config and a short timeline, we do 3 retries max per request, exponential backoff, jitter on top
[03:00] Alex: high level next steps we'll take: Redwood to pull request logs + timeline and look for correlation with kernel / model runtime latencies, Priya will capture GPU queueing / kernel schedule artifacts, and we'll try to reproduce with a controlled burst test w/ same retry pattern
[03:18] Samir: sounds good, one question on rate limits — our gateway has per‑user token bucket, we saw token exhaustion, curious what Redwood's recommended rate‑limit for the hosted endpoint is for this workload?
[03:34] Priya: typically for low latency use we recommend moving to a Dedicated pool when you need predictable throughput — we can model the per‑second token budget based on concurrency; for hosted, we suggest conservative client retry and a 500ms initial backoff for short tasks, but for longer seqs increase initial backoff
[03:55] Evan: ok, but cost is a factor — can we tune timeouts/retries first? we prefer not to move to Dedicated unless required
[04:08] Alex: absolutely, tuning timeouts and retry posture is priority and lower friction; Dedicated is a fallback if we can't get unit economics or latency stability in-hosted
[04:20] Maya: quick: what about caching? we suspect kv cache misses caused a few slower responses, do you have metrics on prefix cache hit rate?
[04:34] Priya: we have aggregated cache hit rates in the console; on our side we saw a drop in prefix cache hit rate around the same timestamp which would cause 2x‑3x latency on first tokens, that plus retries can escalate to 5xxs under burst
[04:52] Evan: is kv cache per model instance or shared? we have multitenant pool so wondering about noisy neighbor effects
[04:59] Priya: it depends on config — Dedicated can give you per‑customer slices so KV cache interference is minimized, hosted can still be tuned but under heavy multi‑tenant bursts you might see collisions
[05:13] Maya: ok makes sense, let's talk observability — what logs will you need from our side to correlate?
[05:21] Alex: request IDs, gateway logs, proxy timeouts, and mapping to client retries; Priya will need GPU metrics and any driver level logs, if you can upload a pcap or tcpdump for the window that would be helpful though we realize that's heavier
[05:38] Evan: we can share access to a trimmed slice of ELK logs and the ingress traces, will paste links in the thread, also we'll add the exact retry config
[05:47] Priya: great, another item — can you confirm SNI and TLS session reuse? we saw some TLS churn in the sample traces which causes extra CPU on the edge
[05:58] Samir: noted, will check TLS settings, interestingly some of our older clients don't support keepalive well so may be opening a ton of connections
[06:10] Alex: ok moving onto repro plan — Priya suggests a controlled burst harness that mirrors your client retry jitter and concurrency, with seq length distribution matching production (p50 ~ 512 tokens, p95 ~ 2k)
[06:30] Priya: yes please, ideally run two variants: one with current proxy retry/timeout, one with slightly elevated initial backoff (500ms) and reduced max retries, measure 5xx and latency tail
[06:45] Evan: question — can Redwood simulate rate limit headers so we can test client behavior?
[06:52] Priya: we can add synthetic 429s in the harness and run a test, or run tests against a Dedicated reserved pool to see behavior under pressure
[07:02] Maya: if we end up in Dedicated how quick is provisioning? we have concerns about lead time
[07:09] Alex: Dedicated provisioning for a small pool can be done in days typically but for large capacity it's longer; we'll send a short doc on Dedicated sizing and pricing after the call
[07:23] Samir: any initial root cause thoughts? you mentioned kernel traces earlier
[07:28] Priya: prelim is three‑way: 1) proxy timeouts + aggressive client retries creating retry storm, 2) temporary KV cache miss on a subset of instances causing tail latency, 3) a small scheduling jitter at the GPU runtime during a hot restart — we need traces to confirm order of events
[07:52] Evan: also the gateway reported a spike in 502s from upstream which aligns to the same window, could be healthcheck flapping under CPU pressure
[08:00] Alex: ok on the logs we saw increased queue depth on the model worker and some worker restarts in that window, but not full crashes — likely a transient scheduling stall
[08:12] Maya: going to the client side, we had some mobile SDKs that surfaced the error to users quickly; what's your recommended client‑side UX for these short incidents?
[08:24] Priya: show a soft retry indicator and avoid immediate user‑facing error for background tasks; for interactive flows show a loading hint and try a single gentle retry, don't cascade retries across layers
[08:35] Evan: we'll also tighten our circuit breaker to avoid heavy client retries; perhaps exponential backoff starting at 500ms and cap retries at 2 for interactive calls
[08:46] Alex: agreed, and on Redwood side we'll add request sampling for full traces in that window and share a csv + timeline doc, link will be posted in the CRM note
[09:00] Maya: any thoughts on rate limiter tuning? we saw token bucket exhaustion and then a sudden refill which caused bursts of allowed traffic
[09:09] Priya: you might want to smooth refill rate or add a small leaky bucket in front to avoid synchronized bursts; also consider token reservation for critical flows
[09:22] Evan: good idea, will prototype smoothing and report back
[09:27] Samir: on the security/compliance side we also want to ensure any log sharing is compliant — can you confirm Redwood's retention and masking defaults for dev logs?
[09:38] Alex: yes, we'll share the security/retention note, default is 30 days for verbose logs but we can provide masked slices and longer retention as an add‑on; full SOC2 docs link will be shared
[09:50] Priya: quick note — when you send logs please include the model alias and request id mapping, sometimes our internal names differ and that causes friction in correlation
[10:00] Maya: we'll annotate the mapping in the thread
[10:07] Alex: ok wrapping up with timeline — Redwood will produce initial log analysis and timeline by end of day tomorrow, Priya to run a repro harness and try the backoff variant, Evan to share proxy config and trimmed traces, Maya to gather client retry behavior and mobile SDK versions
[10:25] Evan: one more thing — do you have guidance on tuning edge‑side timeouts vs upstream? we had idle_timeout 60s and upstream_timeout 10s which sounded odd to us
[10:38] Priya: upstream timeout should generally be > client initial timeout to avoid premature failures; idle_timeout vs keepalive specifics depend on your LB; we'll send recommended snippets for nginx/istio
[10:50] Samir: thanks, we'll try the config changes in canary first
[11:00] Alex: perfect, I'll post the artifacts: 1) timeline csv, 2) initial log sample, 3) Dedicated pricing doc link, and 4) repro harness plan. We'll also schedule a follow up once we have repro results
[11:18] Maya: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround and clarity
